about.title: About PEvO
about.whatIsDescription: PEvO (Publish and Evaluate Openly) is an open platform for scientific publication and interactive peer evaluation. Papers, reviews, and votes are recorded on a permanent public record that no single entity controls, making the entire scientific discourse transparent, permanent, and verifiable.
about.whyDescription: Traditional academic publishing suffers from opaque peer review processes, paywalled access, slow publication cycles, and concentrated gatekeeping power. PEvO addresses these issues by making publication instant, review transparent, and access unrestricted.
about.noPaywallsDesc: All research is freely accessible to everyone, permanently.
about.transparentReviewDesc: Reviews and ratings are publicly recorded and verifiable by anyone.
about.noGatekeepersDesc: Accredited researchers publish directly. No editor bottleneck.
about.immutableRecordDesc: Published work cannot be altered or censored after the fact.
about.howItWorksCaption: PEvO replaces the gatekept journal model with open, transparent publishing and evaluation.
about.step1Desc: Write your paper in Markdown or upload a PDF. Your name and timestamp are permanently recorded on the public record.
about.step2Desc: Accredited researchers write structured peer reviews with ratings on methodology, novelty, clarity, and significance. Anonymous reviewing is supported.
about.step3Desc: The community votes on papers and reviews. Reputation scores are computed transparently from your published activity: publications, reviews, votes, citations, and accreditation status.
about.architectureCaption: PEvO is built on the Hive network and IPFS for permanent, distributed storage that no single entity controls.
about.accreditationDesc: Anyone can read and vote on PEvO. To publish papers and write reviews, researchers verify their identity through an institutional email, ORCID, or vouches from accredited colleagues. Scientists can sign up with just an email and password — no special software required. This accreditation is recorded as a public attestation, building trust without centralized control.
about.openSourceDesc: PEvO is non-profit, AGPL-3.0-licensed, and fully forkable. The reputation algorithm is transparent and configurable. All data lives on a permanent public record that anyone can read. There are no tokens, no paywalls, no vendor lock-in.
about.comparisonSubtitle: PEvO combines the full open, transparent, decentralized stack. Other platforms cover parts well.
about.comparisonFooter: Based on publicly available information as of April 2026. Sci-Hub and Sci-Net are access platforms, not publishing platforms — features outside their scope are marked n/a. Hover over any cell for details.
about.tip_Publishing_pevo: Publish directly to the permanent record — no editorial gate, no waiting
about.tip_Publishing_arxiv: Moderated: submissions screened before posting, some rejections
about.tip_Publishing_scienceopen: Basic screening, some collections are editorially curated
about.tip_Publishing_octopus: Publish any research output instantly, no gatekeeping

about.tip_Ratings_f1000: Structured referee reports with recommendation levels
about.tip_Ratings_scienceopen: Star ratings available, but not mandatory on all content
about.tip_Ratings_octopus: Quality ratings on individual outputs, still evolving
about.tip_Ratings_traditional: Accept/revise/reject decisions — rarely quantitative or public
about.tip_OpenSource_pevo: AGPL-3.0-licensed, all code and algorithms are public and forkable
about.tip_Immutable_pevo: Every publication is a signed transaction on a public, append-only record (Hive)
about.tip_NonProfit_pevo: No fees to publish, read, or review — funded by community
about.tip_NonProfit_arxiv: Free to read and submit, funded by Cornell and grants
about.tip_NonProfit_f1000: Author-side publication fees (APCs) for some services
about.tip_NonProfit_octopus: Free to use, funded by UK Research and Innovation
about.tip_NonProfit_scihub: Free access — operates outside copyright law
about.tip_NonProfit_scinet: Free access with optional token incentives for uploaders
about.tip_NonProfit_traditional: Subscription paywalls or author-pays open access (APCs)
about.tip_Transparent_pevo: All reviews are public and signed (or pseudonymous by choice)
about.tip_Transparent_f1000: Published referee reports visible alongside papers
about.tip_Transparent_scienceopen: Open peer review with published reviewer identities
about.tip_Transparent_octopus: Reviews are published openly alongside research outputs
about.tip_Versioning_pevo: Continuation-chain versioning with linked corrections and diff tracking

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about PEvO and open science.
faq.a1: PEvO (Publish and Evaluate Openly) is an open platform for scientific publication and interactive peer evaluation. Papers, reviews, and votes are recorded on a permanent public record that no single entity controls, making the entire scientific discourse transparent, permanent, and verifiable.
faq.a2: Yes. PEvO is completely free — there are no fees for publishing, reviewing, or voting. PEvO is non-profit and open source.
faq.a3: The quickest way is to sign up with your institutional email and a password. PEvO creates an account for you automatically — no extensions or software to install. You can also use an existing Hive account with the Hive Keychain browser extension for full self-custody of your keys. See the Getting Started guide for step-by-step instructions.
faq.a4: A light account lets you sign up with just an email and password. PEvO creates a real account on the Hive network and manages the keys for you, so you can publish and review without installing any software. You receive a recovery phrase at signup — keep it safe. You can upgrade to full self-custody with Hive Keychain at any time, and PEvO will no longer hold your keys.
faq.a5: Hive Keychain is a browser extension that securely stores your account keys and signs your publications and reviews locally. Your private keys are never shared with PEvO. Keychain is optional — light accounts work without it — but it gives you full control over your keys.
faq.a6: PEvO is built on Hive, an open network designed for content and social applications. It processes updates in 3 seconds, has no transaction fees, and stores data across thousands of independent nodes worldwide. If PEvO the website disappeared tomorrow, every paper and review would still exist on every Hive node.
faq.q7: What is accreditation and why do I need it?
faq.a7: Accreditation verifies that you are an active researcher. It is required to publish papers and write reviews. You can get accredited by verifying your institutional email, by linking your ORCID iD (if you have published works on record), or by receiving vouches from accredited colleagues (Web of Trust).
faq.q8: Can I import papers from other platforms?
faq.a8: Yes. You can register existing papers from arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, or ResearchGate by pasting a URL or identifier. The paper stays on its original platform — PEvO creates a reference so it can receive peer reviews and ratings here.
faq.a9: Papers are always attributed to the publishing account. However, peer reviews can be submitted anonymously through a platform proxy account. The reviewer's identity is stored encrypted and can only be revealed through a governance process.
faq.a10: Papers are stored permanently on Hive and cannot be deleted. This is by design — it ensures the integrity of the scientific record. If you need to revise a paper, you can publish an updated version that links to the original. All previous versions remain accessible, and reviews stay attached to the version they were written for.
faq.a11: Papers can be written directly in Markdown (with LaTeX math support) or uploaded as PDFs. You can also attach supplementary files such as images, datasets, and ZIP archives. PDFs and attachments are stored on IPFS for permanent, distributed access.
faq.q12: How does the reputation system work?
faq.a12: Reputation scores are computed from your published activity: the number and quality of publications, peer reviews written, citations received, community votes, and accreditation status. Votes from higher-reputation researchers carry more weight. The algorithm is transparent, reproducible, and configurable.
faq.a13: Yes. PEvO is AGPL-3.0-licensed and fully forkable. The source code, reputation algorithm, and all data are public. There are no tokens, no paywalls, and no vendor lock-in.
faq.q14: How do I cite a PEvO paper?
faq.a14: Each paper has a unique identifier (author/permlink) and a permanent URL. You can export citations in APA, BibTeX, or RIS format directly from the paper page, or cite PEvO papers like any other online publication.

landing.howItWorksDescription: PEvO replaces the traditional journal model with transparent, open publishing and evaluation.
landing.step1Description: Write your paper in Markdown or upload a PDF. It is published to the permanent record - timestamped, permanent, and yours.
landing.step2Description: Accredited researchers write structured peer reviews with ratings on methodology, novelty, clarity, and significance.
landing.step3Description: Your reputation score is computed transparently from your published activity: publications, reviews, citations, and community votes.
landing.whyPevoDescription: Traditional academic publishing is broken. PEvO fixes it.
landing.noPaywallsDesc: All research is freely accessible to everyone, permanently stored on an open public record.
landing.transparentReviewDesc: Every review and rating is publicly recorded, verifiable by anyone. No more opaque editorial decisions.
landing.noGatekeepersDesc: Accredited researchers publish directly. No months-long editorial bottlenecks.
landing.immutableRecordDesc: Published work cannot be altered, retracted silently, or censored after the fact.
landing.openSourceDesc: AGPL-3.0-licensed, non-profit, fully forkable. The reputation algorithm is transparent and configurable.
landing.decentralizedDesc: Built on an open protocol - like email, anyone can access the data. No single point of failure, no single entity in control.
landing.ctaDescription: Start publishing, reviewing, and building your scientific reputation today.
